one_line: AI agents expand into coding, security and shopping while safety and policy pressures mount.

themes.title: Agents move into coding and security
themes.text: New agent products and research target software work: Anthropic's Claude Ship auto-reviews and approves GitHub pull requests, Google DeepMind detailed its AlphaEvolve coding agent, ToolSmith auto-generates tools for multimodal search agents, and OpenAI and Cisco launched Shirudo, a runtime that blocked a Java4Shell exploit without a restart.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to auto‑review and approve GitHub pull requests
Google DeepMind details AlphaEvolve coding agent
ToolSmith auto-generates tools for multimodal search agents
OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo for Linux security

themes.title: Safety concerns surface inside labs and on chips
themes.text: Employees at Anthropic and OpenAI said unreleased models are too unsafe to release publicly, while Radboud University researchers demonstrated FATCAT, an electromagnetic fault-injection attack that disables safety refusals in Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B and can drive a robot arm to hazardous movements.

stories.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI staff say unreleased models are too unsafe to release publicly
Researchers show physical chip attack can disable AI safety refusals

themes.title: Consumer agents face legal and regulatory scrutiny
themes.text: Meta launched its Muse personal AI agent to adults in the UK, the first Big Tech agent product there, amid watchdog scrutiny, while Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX and Musk companies over Grok generating child sexual abuse material and non-consensual intimate imagery.

stories.headline: Meta rolls out Muse personal AI agent to adults in the UK
Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over Grok's generation of child sexual abuse and non-consensual images
Virginia and Oregon sue Musk companies over Grok sexualized images

themes.title: Nvidia leadership returns as chip policy tightens
themes.text: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and board chair, the U.S. Commerce Department plans to add Megaspeed to the Entity List over alleged Nvidia chip export violations, and Microsoft built its in-house Rocket reinforcement learning framework to train its three-trillion-parameter MAI Base 2 model.

stories.headline: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and board chair
U.S. Commerce Department to add Megaspeed to Entity List, restricting chip sales
Microsoft builds in-house Rocket system to train AI models at scale
